Method of Attack: Phishing campaigns using spoofed domains and fake social media personas to deliver malware payloads via legitimate file-sharing services
Initial delivery via document exploiting CVE-2021-40444, later via ISO archives containing DLLs and LNK shortcuts
Custom loader DLL dropping Bumblebee malware that uses WMI to gather system information and exfiltrate data to C2
Bumblebee receives commands and downloads additional payloads such as Cobalt Strike
Impacted Systems: Corporate networks targeted by phishing campaigns
Attack Vector: Large-scale phishing emails with spoofed domains and fake LinkedIn personas
Malware download links sent via legitimate file-sharing services like TransferNow, TransferXL, WeTransfer, OneDrive
Indicators of Compromise: Use of spoofed domains registered on different TLDs (.us, .co, .biz)
Malware payloads delivered via TransferNow, TransferXL, WeTransfer, OneDrive
Exploitation of Microsoft MSHTML vulnerability CVE-2021-40444
ISO files containing DLLs and LNK shortcuts
Bumblebee malware communicating with C2 servers
